chunks: You cause the night to enter the day, and You cause the day to enter the night, and You bring forth the living from the dead, and You bring forth the dead from the living, and You provide whomsoever You will without reckoning.

key_terms.تُولِجُ: You cause to enter / You merge

ai.seo_question: What are the four divine actions mentioned in Surah Al-Imran verse 27 regarding God's power and provision?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores Allah's absolute sovereignty over cosmic cycles and resurrection, serving as a precursor to the concept of divine authority (Wilayah) held by the Imams. The phrase 'without account' (bi-ghayr hisab) highlights the boundless nature of divine grace, distinguishing it from transactional human logic. This alternation of light and darkness is often interpreted as a metaphor for the transition between spiritual ignorance and knowledge through the guidance of the Ahl al-Bayt.
